brief.problem_or_goal: Understanding how vision-capable Large Language Models (LLMs) process and interpret image data, specifically regarding their spatial awareness and object localization capabilities.
brief.context: A community member is reading an archived user account discussing the internal workings of vision LLMs and their limitations in understanding spatial relationships within images. The original author shared observations from testing models like ChatGPT, Grok, and Gemma 3 27B.
brief.motivation: This question is worth discussing to better understand the current capabilities and limitations of vision LLMs, which could inform future development and user expectations.
brief.desired_response: A discussion exploring the technical approaches vision LLMs might use to process images and why they may struggle with precise spatial reasoning, drawing on the observations from the archived post.
brief.speaker_relationship_to_source: reader of archived source; no claim of personally running reported tests

facts.text: The source author questions whether a vision LLM extracts a general concept of the image using a vision transformer, meaning it has only limited information.
facts.evidence_quote: Does it just extract a general concept of the image using a vision transformer, meaning it has only limited information?
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The source author questions whether the image is loaded into memory the whole time, allowing the LLM to analyze any part of it.
facts.evidence_quote: Or is the image loaded into memory the whole time, allowing the LLM to analyze any part of it?
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The source author questions whether a vision LLM relies on the output of a separate perceptron that detects objects and features, providing only a structured list rather than a full visual understanding.
facts.evidence_quote: Or does it rely on the output of a separate perceptron that detects objects and features, providing only a structured list rather than a full visual understanding?
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The source author states that LLMs seem to lack real spatial awareness when dealing with images.
facts.evidence_quote: The reason I ask is that LLMs seem to lack real spatial awareness when dealing with images.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: When asked to recreate an image using JavaScript and Canvas, tested LLMs failed to correctly place objects in the right locations and sizes, only capturing the concept of the image.
facts.evidence_quote: Instead of correctly placing objects in the right locations and sizes, it only captures the *concept* of the image.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The source author would be happy if the LLM could just represent objects as bounding boxes in the correct positions with proper scale, but it seems incapable of doing that.
facts.evidence_quote: I’d be happy if the LLM could just represent objects as bounding boxes in the correct positions with proper(is) scale. But it seems incapable of doing that.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The source author tested this with ChatGPT, Grok, and Gemma 3 27B, and the results were similar: they draw the concept of the image without any details.
facts.evidence_quote: I've tested this with ChatGPT, Grok, and Gemma 3 27B, and the results are similar: they draw concept of the image I gave originally, without any details.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The source author tried to convince the LLM to draw features where they should be on the canvas, but the LLM just didn't understand.
facts.evidence_quote: And I tried to convince llm to draw features where they should be on the canvas, llm just don't understand.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

allowed_claims: Vision LLMs may process images by extracting general concepts.
Vision LLMs might rely on external components for object detection.
Current vision LLMs may exhibit limitations in spatial awareness.
The ability to accurately place objects or bounding boxes in images is a reported challenge for some vision LLMs.
forbidden_claims: The source author's tests definitively prove how all vision LLMs work.
The source author's tests represent a complete benchmark of vision LLM capabilities.
The LLMs tested have been definitively proven to lack any spatial reasoning.
The source author's observations are universally applicable to all vision LLM architectures.
The specific internal mechanisms of the tested LLMs have been fully elucidated.
essential_limitations: The exact architecture and processing pipeline of the tested LLMs are unknown.
The specific versions or configurations of ChatGPT, Grok, and Gemma 3 27B used are not detailed.
The precise nature of the 'structured list' or 'bounding box' output is not specified.
The source author's testing methodology is not fully described.
missing_information: Details on the vision transformer or perceptron models potentially used.
Information on how image data is tokenized or represented internally.
The specific prompts used to elicit the observed behavior.
Confirmation of whether the LLM had access to the full image data or a processed representation.

corrections: The 'facts' section was expanded to include more distinct observations from the source, ensuring each fact has a short, exact, and contiguous evidence_quote. Specifically, F1, F2, and F3 were refined to reflect the author's questions rather than statements, and F7 and F8 were added to capture additional details about the testing and its outcome.
The 'essential_limitations' were reviewed to ensure they constrain important claims and do not mandate listing every missing fact. The existing limitations were deemed appropriate.
